findings.evidence: Binomial.lean:131 `one_mem_ringChooseSpan`, :145 `mul_mem_ringChooseSpan`, :168-179 the hand-rolled `Subring.closure_induction` whose `one`/`mul` cases are precisely those two lemmas; the PR description itself lists `ringChooseSubring` and `ringChooseSubring_le_kostantForm`, and the module doc (:21-22) asserts the span "is already a subring" — neither exists in the code.
findings.fix: Define `ringChooseSubring (r : R) : Subring R` with carrier `ringChooseSpan r` (fields: `one_mem_ringChooseSpan`, `mul_mem_ringChooseSpan`, and the `AddSubgroup` closure properties). Then the forward inclusion is `Subring.closure_le.2 (Set.range_subset_iff.2 (ringChoose_mem_ringChooseSpan r))` instead of the 9-line induction, and KostantForm can state `ringChooseSubring (ι ℚ (h i)) ≤ kostantForm e h` directly via `kostantForm_le_iff`/`Subring.closure_le`.
findings.issue: `one_mem_ringChooseSpan` and `mul_mem_ringChooseSpan` are exactly the extra `Subring` fields over `ringChooseSpan`, but no `Subring` is assembled; consequently lines 168-178 re-prove "the span is a subring" inline via `Subring.closure_induction` (mem/zero/one/add/neg/mul cases), and downstream statements are forced to the subgroup level (`ringChooseSpan_le_kostantForm : … ≤ (kostantForm e h).toAddSubgroup`, KostantForm.lean:175).

summary: The calc proof of `choose_mul_choose` and the closure inductions are sound and readable, but the subring content is never bundled, so `toAddSubgroup_subringClosure_range_ringChoose` re-derives it by hand with a `Subring.closure_induction` that a bundled `Subring` makes unnecessary.
